literal.prompt: Какой тип морского льда образуется, когда рыхлые кристаллы фразиля в бурной воде слипаются в диски?

literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC describes frazil crystals accumulating into slushy circular disks in rough water and raised edges from wave impacts; WMO independently identifies pancake ice as a sea-ice form. The stem asks for the exact taxonomy label, not a visible-shape wordplay clue.

literalGroups.literal: Это блинчатый лёд. В бурной воде кристаллы фразиля собираются в рыхлые диски, которые при смерзании образуют сплошной ледяной покров.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC says rough-water frazil accumulates into pancakes and that the pancakes eventually cement into a coherent sheet.

literalGroups.literal: Игловидные кристаллы фразиля появляются при начале замерзания морской воды, всплывают и срастаются в ледяной лист.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC says needle-like frazil crystals form as ocean water begins freezing, float, accumulate, and bond into sheets.

literalGroups.literal: Блинчатый лёд образует преимущественно округлые диски диаметром 30 см–3 м; волны сталкивают их и приподнимают края.
literalGroups.primaryGround: WMO gives pancake ice pieces a 30 cm–3 m range; NSIDC describes wave impacts raising their edges.

literalGroups.literal: Нилас — тонкая упругая сплошная корка морского льда.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC describes nilas as a continuous thin sheet developing from grease ice; WMO calls it a thin elastic crust under 10 cm.

literalGroups.literal: Припай — морской лёд, прикреплённый к берегу или дну.
literalGroups.primaryGround: WMO defines fast ice as sea ice attached to the shore or ocean floor.

fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.grammar: The “Какой тип ...?” construction accepts each option as a sea-ice type label; all four labels are concise and grammatically compatible.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.plausibilityUniqueKeyAndNoteTruthUsefuln: The label “ледяные иглы” denotes needle-like frazil crystals, an initial form; it is not the later disk form asked for. Its note accurately teaches this option. NSIDC L83-L88.

correctNoteNewFact.newFact: WMO specifies that pancake-ice pieces are predominantly circular and 30 cm to 3 m in diameter.
correctNoteNewFact.whyNew: The proposed stem does not mention a size, and the correct label does not state one; this gives the reader a concrete scale for the named ice form.

entries.absoluteDifficulty: HARD remains appropriate by the frozen assignment: a general adult must know the specific sea-ice formation sequence linking frazil accumulation in rough water to pancake ice.
